naming_notes: Oklahoma City Thunder / Patrick Ewing (appears in 2 statements): Ewing played for the Seattle SuperSonics (2000-01), the franchise that became the Thunder, but never played in Oklahoma City. Franchise-relocation naming issue.

Washington Nationals / Pedro Martinez and Pete Rose: both played for the Montreal Expos (Pedro 1994-97, Rose 1984), the franchise that became the Nationals, but neither ever played as a Washington National. Franchise-relocation naming issue.
Indianapolis Colts / Johnny Unitas: played only for the Baltimore Colts; same franchise, pre-relocation naming issue.
Arizona Cardinals / Jim Thorpe: played for the Chicago Cardinals (1928); same franchise, pre-relocation naming issue.
Atlanta Braves / Babe Ruth and Cy Young: Ruth played for the Boston Braves (1935) and Young for the 1911 Boston Rustlers (Braves franchise); same franchise, pre-Atlanta naming issue.
St. Louis Cardinals / Cy Young: played for St. Louis 1899-1900 (Perfectos/early Cardinals); technically fits the franchise and the 1900 team name, but predates the modern identity.
Boston Red Sox / Cy Young: team was the Boston Americans for most of his tenure (1901-08); the Red Sox name was adopted in his final Boston season, so this fits but is era-sensitive.

Dominican Republic Athletes / Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (appears in 4 statements): born in Montreal, Canada; raised in the Dominican Republic, identifies as Dominican and committed to the DR for the WBC, so the categorization is defensible but birthplace-technical.
Sweden Athletes / William Nylander: born in Calgary, Canada; Swedish citizen who represents Sweden internationally, so the categorization is standard but birthplace-technical.
